QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_62

question.text: For pass-through eligible income (other than business income) of a Category I/II AIF, investors must report it in:

answer.text: Their own tax returns, since the income retains its character and is taxed directly in the investors' hands

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM XIX-A (pp. 254, 258), under Section 115UB of the Income-tax Act, Category I and II Investment Funds enjoy pass-through status for non-business income. The eligible income retains its character and proportion and is taxed directly in the investors' hands as if they had invested directly. The Trap: The fund manager does not report the income on the investor's behalf, and the income is not exempt at the investor level for non-business pass-through items. Pass-through specifically excludes business income, which is taxed at the fund level and exempt for investors. Note: Investors should rely on the Form 64C/64D statement issued by the fund to file their returns correctly, ensuring the income head and proportion match what the fund reports.
